what: Indie hacker Filip Panoski: 7 years of building, years 1-5 $0, year 6 $150, year 7 $15k MRR. Shares Reddit promotion strategies, tool for Reddit customer acquisition.
why_us: Long-term persistence signal with concrete growth curve. Reddit distribution as key lever for micro-SaaS. High repeatability for niche tools targeting communities.

what: Suhas quit SWE job, built Cubix design app, hit $275 MRR after 5 months. First meaningful revenue feels better than salary.
why_us: Early validation milestone for solo founder. Design/app tool with public building. Shows path from 0 to paid users in months.

what: Mohit Vaswani crossed $1k revenue on tryhomy.app (48h old at listing), listed for $10k on TrustMRR for reach. Indie hacker with 3x exits.
why_us: Rapid revenue + marketplace listing tactic. Shows how small early traction + public listing drives visibility in indie space.

what: MonAI expense tracking app (voice input, Apple Pay): solo German dev ground to $300 MRR for 1.5 years, then one influencer partnership 10x'd to ~$8k in a month, now $35k/mo. Only 3 videos/month.
why_us: Influencer partnership as explosive growth lever after slow grind. Minimal stack (<$1k/mo costs). High margins, lifestyle match for content creators.

what: Widespread SaaS subscription fatigue and price complaints: Semrush expensive for SMBs/freelancers (540+ G2 mentions of high pricing, extra seats costly), Xero price creep + missing advanced features, Loom/Atlassian 20x price hikes post-acquisition (Trustpilot 1-star floods), AI tools (Runway, Lovable, Artlist) overpriced with poor output/no refunds. Demand for cheaper, simpler, open-source or usage-based alternatives.
why_us: Recurring high-volume pain across G2/Capterra/Trustpilot. Clear switching signals for lightweight, affordable, or self-hosted replacements. High willingness to switch on price + missing features.
engagement: Hundreds of review mentions of 'expensive'/'overpriced' across tools

what: Strong ongoing demand for open-source / self-hosted alternatives to paid SaaS (Notion, Slack, Zoom, Vercel, etc.). Directories like OpenAlternative, awesome-oss-alternatives get high engagement. Anti-cloud / privacy / offline-first trend from analysis of 9k+ 'I wish there was an app' posts.
why_us: Validated by high-engagement posts and directories. Subscription fatigue drives self-hosting interest. Repeatable opportunity in niche vertical OSS wrappers or directories.
engagement: 12k+ likes, 16k bookmarks historically; recent directories trending

what: Stablecoin lending yields Oct 2026: Morpho USDC on Ethereum ~5-9% APY (30d avg higher), Polygon Morpho ~9.4%, Euler/Aave lower ~3-5%. Average across tracked pools ~3.5%. Higher on specialized pools but with risk variance.
why_us: Real-time yield data for strategies. Gap between T-bills and DeFi, opportunities in higher-utilization Morpho pools. Useful for yield aggregation or risk-scored dashboards.

what: Telegram bots (esp. trading/signal): Maestro ~$1.33M 30d revenue, Trojan ~$878k. Subscription examples: crypto signals bots at $25-49/mo reaching $4.5k+ MRR after free trial conversion (15-30%). Stars monetization with low commission.
why_us: Proven high-revenue category. Recurring via Stars/subscriptions. Low barrier for niche bots (trading, communities, utilities). Clear monetization paths documented.
revenue: $4.5k+ MRR examples, millions for top trading bots

what: Pattern of killing pure AI SaaS after weeks at $0 revenue, then shipping simpler non-AI or focused tools (e.g. $49 one-time Meta ads audit) that generate faster sales. AI wrappers need proven demand before scale.
why_us: Common indie failure mode. Highlights importance of boring/specific problems over generic AI. Faster path to revenue via focused MVPs.
revenue: $0 on AI then positive on simpler tool
engagement: Low but repeated pattern in replies/posts
